config.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane)

intro.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that solves the Maximum Subarray lesson using Kadane's Algorithm. You will learn to find the contiguous subarray within a one-dimensional array of numbers that has the largest sum. The core programming concept is dynamic programming, where you efficiently compute the maximum sum by iterating through the array only once. You will use fundamental JavaScript constructs like loops, variables, and conditional statements to implement the algorithm. This lesson will help you understand how to optimize solutions by avoiding unnecessary re-computation, a key skill in algorithm design.
intro.usecase: The Kadane's algorithm for finding the maximum subarray sum is essential in financial and data analysis applications. For instance, stock trading dashboards use it to identify the most profitable consecutive trading days within a given period. Data analytics platforms apply it to find periods of peak user engagement or highest sales in time-series data. Developers implement this algorithm in budgeting tools to determine the best consecutive months for investment returns, making it a practical solution for optimizing sequential data analysis in real products.

objectives: Implement the Kadane's algorithm to find the maximum subarray sum in a given array.
Initialize and update variables to track current and maximum sums during iteration.
Manipulate array indices and values to compute subarray sums efficiently.
Construct a function that returns the maximum subarray sum for any input array.
Apply conditional logic to reset the current sum when it becomes negative.
Integrate the algorithm into a complete JavaScript function with proper input and output handling.
Control the iteration process through the array using a loop structure.

content.body: Welcome! Today we'll solve a classic lesson: finding the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray. This is called the Maximum Subarray lesson, and we'll learn Kadane's Algorithm to solve it efficiently. By the end, you'll be able to find the best segment of numbers in any array.
content.title: Welcome

content.body:
• Apply Kadane's Algorithm to find maximum subarray sums.
• Implement the algorithm using a single pass through the array.
• Explain why tracking current and global maxima is efficient.
• Recognize when this approach beats checking every possible subarray.
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: What you just did was examine different segments manually. For small arrays, you might check every possible subarray. That's the brute force approach—it works but becomes very slow as arrays grow.
content.title: What you did

content.body: When the array has 10,000 numbers, checking every possible subarray means checking millions of combinations. That's too slow for real applications. We need a smarter method that finds the answer in one pass. Can't figure it out? Click Show me on the next step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: Remember what we have already seen. Instead of checking all subarrays, we can track the best sum ending at each position as we move through the array. Show the learner how to use a lookup structure (like variables) to remember the best sums we've computed so far and avoid re-scanning.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Think of it like keeping a notebook where we write down the best running total we've seen so far, and update it at each step.

content.body: We'll use Kadane's Algorithm. It works by maintaining two variables: one tracks the maximum sum of subarrays ending at the current position, and another tracks the global maximum seen so far.
content.title: The approach
content.illustratedExample:
Walkthrough with [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1]:
Start: currentMax = -2, globalMax = -2
At 1: currentMax = max(1, -2+1) = 1, globalMax = 1
At -3: currentMax = max(-3, 1-3) = -2, globalMax = 1
At 4: currentMax = max(4, -2+4) = 4, globalMax = 4
At -1: currentMax = max(-1, 4-1) = 3, globalMax = 4
At 2: currentMax = max(2, 3+2) = 5, globalMax = 5
At 1: currentMax = max(1, 5+1) = 6, globalMax = 6
Result: 6

content.body:
1. Initialize two variables: currentMax and globalMax, both set to the first element.
2. Loop through the rest of the array.
3. For each number, update currentMax to be the maximum of the number itself or currentMax + number.
4. Update globalMax to be the maximum of globalMax and currentMax.
5. After the loop, globalMax holds the answer.

content.body: Congratulations! You've learned and implemented Kadane's Algorithm for the Maximum Subarray lesson. Remember: we track the best sum ending at each position (currentMax) and the overall best (globalMax). This single-pass approach is much faster than checking all subarrays. Keep practicing with different arrays to solidify your understanding!
